Yes, global management of colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases at the same centre can improve results. This approach allows for a multidisciplinary team of specialists, including surgeons, oncologists, and radiologists, to work together to develop a comprehensive treatment plan. 

By managing both the primary tumour and liver metastases at the same centre, patients can benefit from:

1. Coordinated care: A unified treatment plan can be developed, taking into account the latest diagnostic and therapeutic options.
2. Reduced delays: Simultaneous management can reduce the time between diagnosis and treatment, improving outcomes.
3. Improved communication: A single centre can facilitate better communication among healthcare providers, ensuring that all aspects of care are considered.
4. Enhanced patient experience: Patients can receive comprehensive care in one location, reducing the need for multiple referrals and travel.

Studies have shown that global management of colorectal cancer with synchronous liver metastases at the same centre can lead to improved survival rates, reduced morbidity, and enhanced quality of life.
